title: Bigfoot filmmaker Roger Patterson's widow has died, aged 86
excerpt: One of the last people alive who might have known the full story behind the controversial footage has passed away.
content:

By T.K. Randall
November 15, 2026


Image: AI-generated (Bing AI / Dall-E 3)

One of the last people alive who might have known the full story behind the controversial footage has passed away.

News outlets in the cryptozoology community have this week reported on the sad death of Patricia Patterson - the 86-year-old widow of Roger Patterson and mother to three adult children.

Her passing marks the end of an era with regard to the Bigfoot phenomenon as her husband was behind arguably the most controversial piece of cryptozoological footage ever made.

Filmed in 1967 in Northern California, the Patterson-Gimlin film, which offers a clear view of a large bipedal ape-like creature walking along a creek bed, has long attracted the attention of Bigfoot enthusiasts and skeptics alike.

Many have argued that the creature in the footage is simply a person wearing a costume, while others remain adamant that it represents genuine evidence that Bigfoot is the real deal.

Disagreement over the nature of the clip has been ongoing for almost 60 years.

More recently, though, a new documentary by filmmaker Marq Evans claims to have indisputably exposed the footage as an "incredible hoax".

Entitled Capturing Bigfoot, the documentary includes previously unseen footage to help make the case that the creature filmed that day in 1967 by Patterson and Gimlin was a person in a costume.

"It took me maybe nine months to realize what we really had," said Evans.

"What we eventually found out is that [this new footage] represented a trial run, a rehearsal that was never discarded."

Exactly how much Roger Patterson's wife knew of the incident remains unclear, but given that both she and Roger (who died in 1972) have now passed, we will perhaps never know for sure exactly what went on behind the scenes and exactly how and why the infamous footage came to be.
